findings.claim: Collapsible heading 'Investigating SHC (PAG P3)'.
findings.truth: The specific heat capacity practical is Practical Activity Group P5 (Energy). PAG P3 is Motion.
findings.evidence: spec P1.2d/P1.2f practical suggestions: 'Investigation of the specific heat capacity of different metals or water using electrical heaters and a joulemeter. (PAG P5)'; PAG table: P5 Energy, example 'Determine the specific heat capacity of a metal'; P3 Motion, example 'Investigate acceleration of a trolley down a ramp'

findings.claim: Flashcard answer 'PAG P3.' for 'Name the PAG associated with investigating specific heat capacity.'
findings.truth: PAG P5.
findings.evidence: spec PAG table, P5 Energy; P1.2d practical suggestion (PAG P5)

findings.claim: 'Fusion is the energy to change from solid to liquid; vaporisation is solid to gas'.
findings.truth: Vaporisation is the change from liquid to gas. Solid to gas is sublimation.
findings.evidence: spec P1.2a lists melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing and sublimating; settled fact

findings.claim: Practice question data (36 000 J, 2.0 kg, 18 degC rise) gives the specific heat capacity of iron as 1000 J/(kg degC).
findings.truth: The accepted specific heat capacity of iron is about 450 J/(kg degC). The energy value is changed to 16 200 J so the answer is 450 J/(kg degC).
findings.evidence: recomputation: 16 200 / (2.0 x 18) = 450; settled value for iron ~450 J/(kg degC)

findings.claim: 'Why does water have a high specific heat capacity make it useful in central heating systems?'
findings.truth: The question is ungrammatical. It should read 'Why does water's high specific heat capacity make it useful in central heating systems?'
findings.evidence: reads wrongly on the card

findings.claim: Collapsible heading 'Investigating Hooke's Law (PAG P5)'.
findings.truth: The springs practical is PAG P2 (Forces). PAG P5 is Energy.
findings.evidence: spec P2.3c practical suggestion: 'Investigation of forces on springs - Hooke's law. (PAG P2)'; PAG table P2 Forces, example 'Investigate the effect of forces on springs'

findings.claim: 'You need to know the shape for three key components (PAG P7)'.
findings.truth: I-V characteristics is PAG P6 (Circuit components). PAG P7 is series and parallel circuits.
findings.evidence: spec P3.2g practical suggestion: 'Investigation of I-V characteristics of circuit elements. (PAG P6)'; PAG table P6 example 'Investigate the I-V characteristics of circuit elements'

findings.claim: 'The Earth itself produces a magnetic field ... which is why a compass needle points towards geographic north.'
findings.truth: A compass needle points towards magnetic north, which is not in the same place as the geographic North Pole.
findings.evidence: spec P4.1 common misconceptions: 'Learners often do not know that the geographic and magnetic poles are not located in the same place'; P4.1d

findings.claim: 'Common permanent magnet materials include iron, steel, nickel and cobalt'.
findings.truth: Iron is a magnetic material but soft iron does not keep its magnetism, so it is not used for permanent magnets. Permanent magnets are usually steel. The same lesson later says the soft iron core loses its magnetism when the current stops, so the two statements conflict.
findings.evidence: spec P4.1b (permanent versus induced magnets); electromagnet paragraph in the same lesson; settled fact

findings.claim: Mark scheme for question 2 contains raw LaTeX: \(a = \frac{v - u}{t}\).
findings.truth: The mark scheme is a plain-text field. js/main.js sets it with formatMarkScheme and never calls KaTeX, so the LaTeX shows on screen as raw code. Written as 'a = (v - u) / t'.
findings.evidence: js/main.js lines 460 and 465: marksEl.innerHTML = formatMarkScheme(q.marks); no renderKaTeX call

findings.claim: Mark scheme for question 4 contains raw LaTeX: \(P = I^2R\) and \(P = VI\).
findings.truth: Same plain-text field problem. Written as 'P = I2R' and 'P = VI' in unicode.
findings.evidence: js/main.js lines 460 and 465

findings.claim: Question 6 (pressure at depth, p = h rho g) carries no Higher tier label in the question text.
findings.truth: PM1.3ii and P1.3j are in bold in the spec, so they are tested only on the Higher Tier papers. The article already wraps this content in higher-only; the question needs the same signal. Prefixed '(Higher tier)'.
findings.evidence: bold spec file: '**PM1.3ii** [dagger] pressure due to a column of liquid ...' and '**P1.3j** [dagger] calculate the differences in pressure at different depths in a liquid'

findings.claim: Terminal velocity and the area under a velocity-time graph are assessed in untagged practice questions, a knowledge check and three flashcards, although the article hides both behind higher-only wrappers.
findings.truth: P2.1f and P2.2f are bold, so Higher Tier only. Six assessment items tagged '(Higher tier)'. The article wrappers themselves are correct and are left alone.
findings.evidence: bold spec file: '**P2.1f** interpret enclosed area in velocity-time graphs'; '**P2.2f** describe examples of the forces acting on an isolated solid object or system ... terminal velocity ... skydivers'

findings.claim: Flashcard 'What is inertial mass defined as?' carries no Higher tier label.
findings.truth: P2.2j is bold, so Higher Tier only. The article already wraps the inertial mass section in higher-only. Tag added at the end of the question.
findings.evidence: bold spec file: '**P2.2j** explain that inertia is a measure of how difficult it is to change the velocity of an object and that the inertial mass is defined as the ratio of force over acceleration'

findings.claim: The whole of P4.2 (motor effect, F = BIl, Fleming's left-hand rule, motors, electromagnetic induction) is assessed in untagged practice questions, knowledge checks and flashcards, although the article hides it behind a higher-only wrapper.
findings.truth: Every statement P4.2a to P4.2j and both P4.2 equations are bold, so Higher Tier only. The article wrapper is correct. Twelve assessment items tagged '(Higher tier)'. Note the consequence: after tagging, only two of five knowledge checks and four of eleven flashcards remain available to a Foundation student, so this lesson may need extra Foundation items on P4.1.
findings.evidence: bold spec file: '**PM4.2i**', '**PM4.2ii**', and every statement from '**P4.2a**' to '**P4.2j**' in bold; P4.1a-P4.1g are not bold

findings.claim: Lesson 4 teaches thinking distance, braking distance and total stopping distance inside a unit named Physics Paper 1.
findings.truth: Stopping distance is P8.1e, in Topic P8 Global challenges. The spec puts P8 on Paper 2 (Foundation) and Paper 4 (Higher). Paper 1 and Paper 3 assess P1-P4 and P9 only. Coordinator ruling: keep the teaching here and label it. A scope note is inserted after the Stopping Distance heading naming P8.1 and the second paper.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a: 'Paper 1 assesses content from Topics P1-P4 and P9'; 'Paper 2 assesses content from Topics P5-P8'; P8.1e 'explain the factors which affect the distance required for road transport vehicles to come to rest in emergencies' with 'factors that affect thinking and braking distance and overall stopping distance'

findings.claim: Lesson 7 teaches a.c. versus d.c., the 230 V 50 Hz mains supply, three-pin plug wiring and the National Grid inside a unit named Physics Paper 1.
findings.truth: All of this is Topic P8 Powering Earth, so Paper 2 or Paper 4: a.c./d.c. is P8.2h, mains 50 Hz and about 230 V is P8.2g, live/neutral/earth is P8.2i and P8.2j, the national grid and step-up/step-down transformers are P8.2c to P8.2f. Only the series and parallel circuit rules and the power equations are Paper 1 (P3.2). Coordinator ruling: keep the lesson whole and label it. A scope note is inserted after the AC and DC heading naming P8.2 and the second paper.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a paper mapping; P8.2c-P8.2j

findings.claim: Coverage of P1-P4 across the eight lessons.
findings.truth: Statements in scope for this paper that are taught nowhere in the unit: P1.1a-P1.1c (how the atomic model changed - Thomson, Rutherford with Geiger and Marsden, Bohr; the nucleus and electron picture; typical atom size 1 x 10^-10 m); P1.3d and PM1.3i (pressure x volume = constant for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature - separate-science only, both tiers); P1.3f and P1.3g (a simple model of the atmosphere and why atmospheric pressure falls with height); P1.3h and P1.3i (floating, sinking and upthrust - Higher); P1.3e (doing work on a gas raises its temperature - Higher); PM2.1iii (v squared minus u squared = 2as, both tiers, given on the equation sheet); PM2.1iv (kinetic energy); P2.2e, P2.2g, P2.2h (vector diagrams, resolution of forces, free body diagrams - Higher); P2.2k and PM2.2ii (momentum and conservation of momentum - Higher); P2.2m-P2.2o and PM2.2iii/PM2.2iv (work done and power); PM2.3iv (gravitational potential energy); P2.3o hydraulics. Several of these will sit in the Paper 2 energy lessons, but the spec assesses them on Paper 1. Recommendation: add one Paper 1 lesson on atomic structure plus gas laws and atmospheric pressure, and one on momentum, work, power and energy stores.
findings.evidence: spec topics P1.1, P1.3, P2.1, P2.2, P2.3 read against the eight lesson texts; spec section 2a paper mapping

findings.claim: The lesson teaches fuses, residual current devices and double insulation.
findings.truth: This spec never names a fuse, a circuit breaker or an RCD. P8.2j asks only for the dangers of a live wire and 'the protection offered by insulation of devices'. The content is not wrong, it is extra, and it is also Paper 2 material. No edit; it is useful background.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec for fuse, circuit breaker, residual current, double insulation returns no content statement; P8.2i and P8.2j

findings.claim: Mark scheme for question 6 says 'riding up a hill requires a high gear ratio for more force; riding on flat at speed requires a lower gear ratio'.
findings.truth: This is consistent with the lesson's own definition of gear ratio (larger gear divided by smaller gear), but it is the opposite of everyday cycling language, where a hill is climbed in a low gear. A student could be confused. Not wrong on the lesson's own terms, so no edit.
findings.evidence: lesson definition 'gear ratio - larger gear / smaller gear'; spec P2.3m asks only for ratios and force multiplication

summary: Every worked example, mark scheme number and knowledge check answer key recomputes correctly, and no lesson makes a paper, duration or mark claim. Three Practical Activity Groups were wrong (SHC as P3 not P5, Hooke's law as P5 not P2, I-V characteristics as P7 not P6), one flashcard called vaporisation a solid-to-gas change, one lesson taught that a compass points to geographic north (the misconception the spec itself names), and a practice question implied iron has a specific heat capacity of 1000 J/(kg degC). Every higher-only wrapper in the unit is correctly placed against the bold spec, but the practice questions, knowledge checks and flashcards that test those same bold statements carried no tier label, so twenty of the thirty-three edits add '(Higher tier)'. Two lessons carry Topic P8 material (stopping distance; mains, plugs and the National Grid) that the spec assesses on Paper 2; on the coordinator's ruling both keep the teaching and gain a scope note rather than being moved or split. Several Paper 1 statements are still taught nowhere (F18).
